text:
ashley: heads-up — noticed former contractor alex.j still has access to prod-bucket (data-reader) even after SCIM deprov yesterday. KMS logs show decrypt events at 02:13 UTC. :rotating_light: anyone seen similar?

scim-bot: automated: scim-provisioner corp tenant job failed at 2026-03-18T01:58:12Z, error: missing attribute 'member' for group update, skipping membership sync for user alex.j

samir: can you paste the deprov event from the audit log? scim-pruner ran overnight and reported 0 removals for that tenant.

ashley: pasted log excerpt below — looks like the provisioner created the group object but skipped members.
```
2026-03-18T01:57:59Z INFO scim: applyGroup delta: group=prod-developers, extId=gid-1234
2026-03-18T01:58:12Z WARN scim: missing attribute 'member' in payload, skipping members for user alex.j (uid: u-9987)
2026-03-18T01:58:30Z INFO prober: enqueued user deprovision event uid=u-9987
```

olivia: FYI, we rolled an IdP mapping change last week — IdP started sending "members" (plural) instead of "member" in SCIM patch. We updated the mapping in the SSO app but I guess the provisioner config didn't get the new key.

samir: that would explain it. provisioner treats missing members attr as intentional empty and skips updates. root cause looks like attribute-name drift between IdP and provisioner config. Fix options: 1) revert IdP mapping to send "member" 2) update provisioner mapping to accept both keys and backfill members 3) run targeted removal for deprovisioned users in prod while we backfill.

luis: from a KMS/audit perspective this is high risk — principle still present in IAM binding for key prod-key-01. We should either rotate the key or tighten the key policy to deny principals not in the current active user set until we finish cleanup. Also collecting evidence for the compliance ticket.

ashley: agree. short-term mitigation: samir, can you force-remove alex.j from prod groups and run the pruner backfill? luis — can you apply a key policy condition that denies access from non-org-managed principals for prod-key-01?

samir: on it. test plan first: run a dry-run removal then actual DELETE. commands: 
```
# dry-run
./scim-cli backfill --tenant corp --user u-9987 --groups --dry-run
# delete membership via provisioning API
curl -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://console.redwood.internal/api/v1/groups/gid-1234/members/u-9987"
```
I'll run dry-run now and report.

olivia: after fix we should add a unit/integration test for attribute aliasing (member vs members) and update the IdP mapping checklist in runbook. Also add a monitoring alert for any scim-provisioner mismatches > 5 failures/hour.

luis: key policy patch submitted (temp deny). I updated key policy to add condition: "requester in active_org_principals == true" (internal condition). Rotating key is heavy; let's keep policy short-lived while you verify all deprovs. I'll record the change in the compliance ticket.

samir: dry-run shows: 
```
2026-03-18T02:05:12Z INFO backfill: user u-9987 would be removed from groups: [prod-developers]
```
Proceeding with actual delete.

samir: done — membership deleted and audit event emitted.
```
2026-03-18T02:09:03Z AUDIT membership.delete user=u-9987 group=gid-1234 actor=samir
```

scim-bot: scim-pruner run completed at 2026-03-18T02:14:00Z: removed 1 stale membership(s) for tenant corp.

ashley: thanks all — luis can you confirm KMS logs show no further decrypts by alex.j? will need that for compliance. olivia please file the follow-up: mapping test + runbook item + alert. samir please add a small fix to provisioner to accept both "member" and "members" keys before next deploy.

luis: confirmed: no decrypt events after 02:15 UTC. exported logs to the compliance ticket #C-2247.

samir: created PR with quick tolerant parsing and a unit test for aliasing. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/provisioner/pull/314 (small change, tests added).

olivia: filed follow-ups: RUNBOOK-145 (IdP mapping checklist), MON-502 (scim-provisioner attr-drift alert). cc: @security-triage.

ashley: great work. will schedule a short retrospective tomorrow to avoid repetition. :thumbsup:
